fact_text: The analyst treats passing an international oil price rise through to local pump prices quickly as the most important policy discipline during an oil shock for Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When local fuel prices stay frozen after a global rise, consumers keep buying the same volume and buyers hoard, so the import bill grows far more than the price rise alone would suggest.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Investors expect a government that subsidises fuel for long to be forced to raise prices later, so a prolonged subsidy is itself read as a signal of future price increases.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An oil supply shock raises inflation, but the central bank does not automatically raise policy rates; it judges whether the shock is temporary or likely to persist.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An oil shock that is not passed through, combined with a widening current account deficit and falling reserves, can drive currency devaluation, which then keeps inflation high and forces rate hikes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: About 20 million barrels a day, roughly 20 percent of global oil supply, passes through the Strait of Hormuz.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Saudi Arabia can export about 5 million barrels a day by alternate routes and the UAE can use other ports, so a Hormuz closure would not stop all Gulf oil flows.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A full Hormuz closure is estimated by the analyst as a 10 to 12 million barrels a day supply shock, about 10 percent of global supply, similar in scale to the 1990 disruption.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Countries typically hold about 10 to 30 days of oil supply, so industry starts to feel a supply shock within roughly 20 to 30 days as tankers and gas stop arriving.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The 1990 Iraq-Kuwait crisis put about 5 million barrels a day of supply under threat, roughly 7 to 8 percent of global supply, against global demand of about 66 million barrels a day.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Russia exported roughly 5 to 6 million barrels a day out of about 100 million barrels a day of global output, and also supplied gas to Europe, making the 2022 shock an oil and gas shock.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: During the 1990 oil shock Pakistan raised petrol by up to Rs 20 a litre from a base near Rs 89, and reversed the increase when oil prices eased.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's current account deficit in FY91 was about 1.25 to 1.5 billion dollars, roughly 3 percent of GDP, during the 1990 oil shock that lasted seven to eight months.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The KSE-100 fell at most about 16 percent during the 1990 oil shock, and the market had already corrected before the shock peaked, while trading at roughly 7 to 8 times earnings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's own backtest says entering the KSE-100 about 21 days after the 1990 crisis began, near peak oil prices, returned about 60 percent after one year and about 111 percent after two years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Iraq produced about 3 percent of global oil demand before the 2003 US-Iraq war, and most of the oil price rise came before the invasion rather than during it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: During the 2003 oil shock the State Bank did not raise interest rates, and the rupee appreciated despite higher oil prices because the economy was growing strongly.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The KSE-100 fell about 22 to 23 percent into the 2003 oil shock, starting from a P/E near 8.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's backtest says entering the KSE-100 about 21 to 25 days after the 2003 shock began returned about 89 percent after one year, 155 percent after two years and 321 percent after three years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In 2022 Pakistan delayed passing the oil price rise to consumers for about four months, partly because elections were expected, and the analyst regards this as the main policy error of that shock.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After the 2022 oil shock Pakistan's current account deficit reached about 4 percent of GDP, and reserves were cited at about 16 billion dollars as the external position deteriorated.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the 2022 crisis the rupee weakened sharply and inflation rose above 25 percent; the analyst says the State Bank then had to raise rates, which was the one past oil shock where rate hikes were needed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In 2023 the government passed the oil price shock through to consumers, which kept the current account deficit near 1.5 billion dollars, about 1.5 percent of GDP.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Across the three past oil shocks the KSE-100 corrected roughly 16 to 25 percent, and the analyst reports the drawdown generally formed within the first 20 to 25 days of each shock.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst measures oil-shock investment returns from about 21 to 25 days after the shock begins, arguing that markets price the forward-looking scenario within the first month.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst advises judging oil-shock investments on one, two and three year returns rather than on one to three month volatility, which can be very large in index moves.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the 1999 to 2007 and 2008 to 2017 boom cycles, roughly 4x profit growth combined with about 3x P/E expansion compounded into an index rally of about 10 to 11 times over 7 to 8 years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst applies the rule of 72 to Pakistani companies: average annual profit growth of about 18 percent doubles profits in roughly four years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says the market cycle from 2023 onward closely mirrors the 1999 to 2007 cycle, which also began after a sanctions-driven crisis with low reserves and compressed P/E ratios.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst links Pakistan's fuel price decisions to its IMF programme, which required meeting a June 2026 dollar reserves target.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict ended, the analyst says Pakistan's geopolitical standing rose and the market staged a sharp V-shaped recovery; the June 2025 Iran-Israel war showed a similar fast rebound.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rising Oil Prices & PSX | Risk or Opportunity?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
